title: How to Create an AI Agent with Claude to Run Your Business (Step by Step)
excerpt: The exact step by step system I use to run three companies with an AI
quote: Clarity compounds. The founder who starts every morning already knowing what matters wins the month, the quarter, and the year.
body:
Every morning before my three daughters are awake, an AI agent I built inside Claude has already done my first hour of work for me. It reads what happened overnight across my three companies, checks my calendar, scans my inbox for the messages that actually need me, and hands me a short brief I can read with my coffee in five minutes.

I did not write a single line of code to build it. I did not hire a developer. I did not watch a 4 hour course. If you can write a clear text message, you can build this, and in this post I am going to walk you through exactly how to create an AI agent with Claude, step by step, using the same morning brief agent I use to operate [VIXA](https://www.vixaapp.ai), my dating clarity app for women, [Havenly](https://www.havenly.co), my Gen Z beauty brand built for global retail shelves, and [LUMAPROMPT.AI](https://www.lumaprompt.ai), my human authored prompt platform designed for women.

Grab your coffee. This is a full guide, and by the end of it you will know enough to build your first agent tonight.

## What Is an AI Agent, in Plain English

Let me clear up the buzzword first, because "AI agent" gets thrown around so much online that it has almost stopped meaning anything.

A chatbot answers questions when you ask them. An agent completes work without being asked. That is the entire difference, and it is a big one.

When you use AI the normal way, you are the engine. You open the chat, you think of the question, you type it, you read the answer, you follow up. The AI is smart, but everything still depends on you showing up and driving. An agent flips that. You give it a job once, you connect it to your tools once, you set a schedule once, and from that point on it runs on its own and reports back to you. You go from operating the AI to managing it.

That shift changed how I run my businesses. Instead of me chasing information every morning across email, calendars, project boards, and messages, the information now comes to me, already gathered, already organized, already prioritized. I start the day making decisions instead of hunting for the facts I need to make them.

## What My Morning Brief Agent Actually Does

Every weekday at 6:00 in the morning Eastern time, while I am at the gym, my agent runs on its own and delivers one brief that covers 4 things:

1. My calendar for the day, listed with times, with anything that needs preparation flagged, so a manufacturer call for Havenly never catches me unprepared
2. Overnight emails that need a decision or a reply from me, with the noise filtered out, so newsletters and promotions never touch my attention
3. Anything urgent or stalled across my three companies, from supplier messages for Havenly, to user feedback and reviews for VIXA, to content and writer updates for LUMAPROMPT.AI
4. One suggested top priority for the day, with the reason why, so I start every morning with my first decision already made

Notice what it does not do. It does not answer my emails for me. It does not post for me. It does not make decisions for me. It does one job, gathering and prioritizing, and it does that job extremely well. That focus is deliberate, and it is the first lesson of this entire guide.

## Step 1: Give Your Agent One Clear Job

The biggest mistake I see founders make with AI agents is trying to build one that does everything. An agent that monitors your inbox, writes your content, tracks your competitors, and manages your calendar sounds impressive, and it will do all 4 things badly. Vague scope produces vague output, every single time.

Pick one job. Write it down in one sentence before you touch any software. If you cannot describe the job in one sentence, you are describing two agents, not one.

Here are examples of well scoped agent jobs, any of which would make a great first build: a weekday morning brief like mine, a Friday afternoon summary of the week's sales numbers, a daily list of customer messages and reviews that need answers, a Monday morning roundup of what your top 3 competitors published or launched last week, or a nightly check that flags any invoice or payment that is overdue.

And here is a badly scoped one: "help me manage my business." That is not a job, that is a wish. Agents run on jobs.

![How to create an AI agent with Claude step 1: give your agent one clear job](/images/uploads/step1-one-clear-job.png)

My advice is to start with the morning brief. It touches your real daily operations, you get feedback on it every single day, and it teaches you the skill of writing instructions faster than any other agent because you review its work each morning.

## Step 2: Open Claude and Find Scheduled Tasks

Now the practical part. You will need a paid [Claude](https://claude.ai) plan for this. Scheduled tasks live inside Claude Cowork, the workspace where Claude can take on real work, and they are available on the paid plans, which are Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. The feature has been rolling out in stages, so if you do not see it yet, check the [official Claude help article on scheduled tasks](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork) for the current status.

Here is the path:

1. Open Claude on desktop and go into Cowork
2. Find Scheduled in the left sidebar
3. Click New task

From there you have two options, and I want you to understand both.

The first option is Create with Claude. Claude interviews you with a few multiple choice questions about what you want, proposes a task name, a schedule, and instructions, and you review and click Schedule to confirm. If this is your first agent, use this path. It is the fastest way to learn how these tasks are structured, because Claude essentially shows you what good setup looks like.

The second option is Set up manually. You fill in the task name, the instructions, the approval mode, the frequency, and optionally the model and folder. Once you have built one or two agents, you will probably prefer this path because you will know exactly what you want.

![How to find Scheduled tasks in Claude Cowork to create an AI agent](/images/uploads/step2-find-scheduled-tasks.png)

Here is the detail I love most, and the one that surprises people: these scheduled tasks run in the cloud, not on your machine. Your agent still fires on schedule when your laptop is closed, when you are on a flight, and when you are mid workout at 6:00 in the morning, which is exactly where I am when mine runs. You are not keeping a computer awake to have an assistant. The assistant simply works.

## Step 3: Connect Your Tools

An agent is only as useful as the information it can see, so this step decides whether your brief feels like a chief of staff or a fortune cookie.

In your Claude settings you can connect the tools your business already runs on. These connections are called connectors, and they let Claude securely read the accounts you approve, and only the accounts you approve. For a morning brief, connect these, in this order of importance:

1. Your calendar, because the agent cannot brief you on a day it cannot see
2. Your email, so it can surface the messages that need a decision from you and skip everything else
3. Your team or project tool, such as Slack or monday.com, so it catches what happened overnight and what stalled
4. Your cloud drive, such as Google Drive, if your key documents live there

![Connect your business tools to Claude with connectors when building an AI agent](/images/uploads/step3-connect-your-tools.png)

Two rules I follow on connections, and I want you to steal both. First, connect only what the agent's one job requires. My morning brief agent does not need access to my financial documents, so it does not have it. Second, start with your lower sensitivity sources, live with the agent for a couple of weeks, and expand access as you build trust in how it behaves. You stay in control of every permission, and you can disconnect anything at any time.

## Step 4: Write the Instructions Like You Are Training an Assistant

This is the step where the quality of your agent is truly decided, and it is the step most people rush. I am going to slow down here because this is the part I know best. Writing instructions that get consistently excellent output is the entire craft behind [LUMAPROMPT.AI](https://www.lumaprompt.ai), where my human expert writers author prompts professionally, so consider this section a free masterclass.

Here is the exact structure of my morning brief instructions. Copy it word for word and adjust it to your business:

> You are my morning operations briefer. Every weekday morning, do the following:
>
> 1. Check my calendar for today and list my meetings with times. Flag anything that needs preparation and say what the preparation is.
> 2. Review emails from the last 16 hours. Surface only the ones that need a decision or reply from me. Ignore newsletters, promotions, and anything my team can handle.
> 3. Check my project boards and team messages for anything marked urgent, anything that stalled, and anything a customer is waiting on.
> 4. End with one line: the single most important thing I should do first today, and why.
>
> Format the whole brief so I can read it in under five minutes. Use short sections with clear headers. Be direct. Do not pad it with pleasantries or repeat information I already know.

![Write clear instructions for your Claude AI agent like a job description](/images/uploads/step4-write-the-instructions.png)

Now let me show you why each part is there, because understanding the why is what lets you write your own.

Every strong set of agent instructions does 5 things. It assigns a role, because "you are my morning operations briefer" focuses the agent's judgment better than a bare list of tasks. It specifies what to include, naming each source explicitly rather than saying "check my stuff." It specifies what to exclude, and this is the one everybody skips: the "ignore newsletters and promotions" line is doing as much work as any other sentence, because without exclusions your brief drowns in noise. It defines the format, since "under five minutes, short sections, clear headers" is the difference between a scannable brief and a wall of text. And it demands a decision, because "the single most important thing and why" forces the agent to prioritize instead of just listing, and prioritization is the whole point.

Weak instructions read like "summarize my emails and calendar." Strong instructions read like a job description for a sharp human assistant. Write for the assistant.

## Step 5: Set the Schedule

Choose your frequency: hourly, daily, weekly, weekdays only, or manual. I run mine on weekdays at 6:00 in the morning because that is when I am at the gym and my brain is already planning the day.

![Set the schedule for your Claude AI agent, weekdays at 6:00 in the morning](/images/uploads/step5-set-the-schedule.png)

A tip from experience: schedule the brief for when you will actually read it, not for the earliest possible hour. A brief that lands at 5:00 and gets read at 9:00 is just noise you paid for, and worse, by 9:00 some of it is stale. Match the schedule to your real routine, not your fantasy routine.

And skip weekends unless your business truly runs 7 days. Protect at least one morning where nothing briefs you at all.

## Step 6: Test It, Then Sharpen It for Two Weeks

Run the task manually the first time, before the schedule ever fires, and read the result with a critical eye. Then refine it daily, the way you would coach a new assistant in their first two weeks:

1. If it included things you do not care about, add an exclusion line naming them
2. If it missed something important, name that source or topic explicitly in the instructions
3. If it ran long, give it a hard limit, such as 300 words maximum
4. If the priority suggestion felt generic, tell it what matters to you this quarter so it can weigh things the way you do

![Test and refine your Claude AI agent for two weeks like coaching a new assistant](/images/uploads/step6-test-and-refine.png)

My current morning brief is version 9. Version 1 was decent. Version 9 feels like a chief of staff who has worked with me for a year. The difference was two weeks of 2 minute edits, not any technical skill. This is the part nobody tells you: building the agent takes 20 minutes, and coaching it is what makes it great.

## What to Build Next, Once the Brief Is Running

Run your morning brief for a full month before adding anything, that is my honest advice. But when you are ready, these are the natural next builds, in the order I would do them: a weekly numbers agent that summarizes your sales and key metrics every Friday, a customer voice agent that digests reviews and support messages into themes once a week, and a competitor watch agent that reports what the brands in your space launched, posted, and changed every Monday. One job each. Always one job each.

## What This Actually Changes for You

I am a mother of 3 building three companies at the same time, and I do not have a spare hour every morning to hunt through six apps to find out what matters. My agent gives me that hour back every single day, and it gives me something more valuable than time. I start every day with clarity instead of chaos, and clarity compounds.

That is the same principle I built [VIXA](https://www.vixaapp.ai) on. Clarity is power. Whether it is your inbox or your dating life, the person with organized information makes better decisions than the person guessing.

## Common Questions

**Do I need to know how to code?** No. Everything in this guide happens in plain English inside the Claude interface. If you can write a clear paragraph, you are qualified.

**Which Claude plan do I need?** A paid plan: Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise. Features roll out in stages, so check the [official Claude help article](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork) for the latest.

**Is my business data safe?** You choose exactly which accounts to connect, the agent sees only what you approve, and you can revoke any access whenever you want. Start small and expand as you build trust.

**How long does this take to set up?** About 20 minutes for the first working version, then a few minutes of refinement a day for two weeks. That is the entire investment.

**Can I build more than one agent?** Yes, and eventually you should. But master one first. A single excellent agent beats five mediocre ones every time.

## Your Move

Building your first AI agent takes about 20 minutes tonight. The version of you 30 days from now, who starts every single morning with a clear brief instead of a chaotic inbox, will be very glad you spent them.

If you build one, tell me about it. I share what I am building every week here on [lisahaven.co](https://www.lisahaven.co) and on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lisahaven), and I answer at lisa@vixaapp.ai.

Now go build your first employee that never sleeps.

title: How to Ask ChatGPT Better Questions: It Is Not What You Ask, It Is HOW You Ask
excerpt: Learning how to ask ChatGPT better questions is the fastest way to turn artificial intelligence into a real business partner. It is not what you ask, it is HOW you ask.
body:
If you have ever typed a question into ChatGPT and received an answer that felt generic, flat, or completely off, the problem is almost never the tool. It is the question. Learning how to ask ChatGPT better questions is the single fastest way to turn artificial intelligence from a toy into a business partner, and most people were never taught how to do it. I use artificial intelligence every single day to run three companies as a mother of 3, and here is the truth I built an entire platform around: it is not what you ask, it is HOW you ask.

## Why Your ChatGPT Answers Feel Generic

ChatGPT and Claude respond to exactly what you give them. When you type "write me an Instagram caption," you are asking the tool to guess your brand, your audience, your tone, and your goal all at once. It cannot read your mind, so it averages everything and hands you something that sounds like everyone else. Vague in, vague out. Specific in, specific out. That is the entire game.

## The Four Ingredients of a Better Question

Every high performing prompt contains the same four ingredients. First, a role: tell the tool who to be, such as "act as a retail buyer for a national beauty chain." Second, context: give it your situation, your audience, and your goal. Third, format: tell it exactly what the output should look like, whether that is a table, a script, or three headline options. Fourth, constraints: word count, tone, what to avoid.

When I negotiate with manufacturers for [Havenly](https://www.havenly.co), my Gen Z beauty brand, I never ask "how do I negotiate." I ask "act as a sourcing expert who has negotiated with beauty manufacturers for 20 years, I am a founder ordering my first 10,000 units, give me the five leverage points I have and the exact language to use for each one." Same tool. Completely different result.

## Before and After: A Real Example

Weak question: "Give me marketing ideas for my app."

Better question: "Act as a growth marketer who has launched consumer apps for women. My app helps women get clarity on confusing dating conversations. My audience is women ages 22 to 40 who live on TikTok and Instagram. Give me five launch ideas ranked by cost, with the first step for each one."

The second version took thirty extra seconds to write and saves hours of back and forth. That is the return on asking better.

## The Shortcut: Let Experts Write the Question for You

Here is the honest part. Most people do not have time to become prompt experts, and they should not have to. That is exactly why I built [LUMAPROMPT.AI](https://www.lumaprompt.ai), a premium prompt generator and curated library written by human industry expert writers, designed around how women process information and make decisions. Every prompt is authored by professionals who understand real world outcomes, nothing scraped or machine averaged. It works for ChatGPT and Claude, it eliminates the guesswork, and it lets you skip straight to execution. Better questions, better results, less time wasted.

## Ask Better, Build Faster

You do not need to be technical to get world class answers from artificial intelligence. You need a role, context, a format, and constraints, or you need someone who has already written the question for you. Start with one prompt today and compare the difference yourself. And if you want the shortcut, visit [www.lumaprompt.ai](https://www.lumaprompt.ai) and let expert written prompts do the heavy lifting. For more real time lessons from my journey building three companies, subscribe at [www.lisahaven.co](https://www.lisahaven.co).

title: Why I'm Building in Public Before Revenue
excerpt: Most founders wait until they're making money to talk about their business. I'm building in public before revenue, on purpose. Here's why.

quote.text1: "Both faith and fear ask you to believe in something you cannot see.
quote.author: Lisa Haven

body:
I built three companies before a single one made me a dollar. And instead of hiding until the money shows up, I am building in public before revenue, on purpose.

Most founders do the opposite. They stay quiet, work in private, and only start talking once the numbers look good and the story is safe. By then the hard part is invisible. You see the highlight reel, never the build.

I want you to see the build.

## Why build in public before revenue?

Because self belief is the one asset that never runs out. Money can run out. Momentum can stall. But the belief that I will figure it out is something I control completely, and I refuse to wait for revenue to give me permission to back myself.

I am documenting all three companies in real time: [VIXA](https://www.vixaapp.ai), my dating clarity app for women; [HAVENLY](https://www.havenly.co), my Gen Z makeup remover wipe brand; and [LUMAPROMPT.AI](https://www.lumaprompt.ai), my human written prompt library for women. None of them have to be finished for the journey to be worth sharing.

## Why document the failures and not just the wins?

Because the failures are the part nobody shows, and they are the part that actually teaches. I have launched a business before that did not work. I am not ashamed of it and I am not embarrassed by it. Failing is part of the process, and I am not afraid of it.

The internet is full of after the fact success stories with the messy middle cut out. I would rather give you the honest version. The good, the hard, the ugly, and eventually the amazing outcome. Wins and corrections included.

## What does failing forward actually mean?

It means every stumble and every study session is tuition. Every single day I watch a founder story or a marketing video and I come out sharper. A better founder. A better marketer. Even on a day that looks like nothing happened, I added knowledge I did not have yesterday.

So if one attempt falls short, I have not lost. I have gathered everything I need for the attempt that finally works. You are never standing still as long as you are still learning.

## The part most people will not admit

I love this. I love the work. I love sitting at my computer, sometimes running my laptop and my desktop at the same time on two different tasks, and I am genuinely happy doing it.

Of course I want the outcome. I want to build real wealth and a legacy for my three daughters. But I stopped letting the outcome be the only thing that matters, because when you love the process this much, you have already won the part most people are still chasing.

## The faith underneath all of it

Here is what I believe. Put your whole journey into your daily habits and success becomes a matter of time, not luck. The harder you work, the more you learn. The more you learn, the more doors open. And the more doors open, the closer you get, as long as you do not quit and you do not let one failure write the ending.

That is the faith I have. Not blind hope. Earned conviction, reinforced every day by showing up.

So I will keep building in public before the revenue. I will keep documenting the parts other founders hide. And I will keep believing, out loud, that something is going to work, because it is.

If you are a woman building something of your own, take this with you. You do not have to wait until you have made it to start. Start now. Be seen trying. Invest in yourself now. 💸

title: I "Manifested" Three Companies. Here's the Part the Law of Attraction Crowd Won't Tell You.
excerpt: Everyone sells manifestation like a vending machine. Here's the part
body:
Everyone wants the vision board. Almost nobody wants the invoice that comes with it.

I believe in the law of attraction — the idea that what you focus on, you pull toward you. I've lived it. But I'm going to tell you the part that doesn't fit on a pastel quote graphic: **manifestation is a contract, and the payment is action.** Skip the payment and the vision stays a fantasy forever.

**The Lie They Sell You**

They sell it like a vending machine. Visualize the car, feel the feelings, repeat the affirmation, and the universe delivers it to your driveway while you sleep.

That's not law of attraction. That's a coping mechanism dressed up as a strategy. The women selling you that version are usually selling you something else right behind it.

Here's the real version: belief is the ignition, not the engine. It gets you to start. It does not drive the car.

**What the Law of Attraction Actually Is**

Strip away the mysticism and there's something real underneath. When you obsess over a specific outcome, your brain quietly reorganizes around it. You start noticing opportunities you used to walk past. You hear the one sentence in a podcast that unlocks a decision. You spot the gap in a market — like a makeup wipe nobody built for Gen Z, which became **HAVENLY** ([www.havenly.co](https://www.havenly.co)).

Clarity is a filter. When you decide exactly what you're building, the world starts sorting itself into "useful" and "noise." That's not magic. That's focus doing what focus does. But it only switches on when the vision is specific enough to be uncomfortable.

**Action Is the Rent You Pay on the Vision**

I did not affirm three companies into existence. I built them.

**VIXA** ([www.vixaapp.ai](https://www.vixaapp.ai)), the artificial intelligence dating clarity app — software that reads patterns and gives women real answers — exists because I sat with developers and architected it screen by screen. **LUMAPROMPT.AI** ([www.lumaprompt.ai](https://www.lumaprompt.ai)) exists because I wrote, refined, and shipped. Every "manifestation" in my life has a paper trail of 3am work behind it.

The universe does not reward the woman who wants it most. It rewards the woman who moves most in the direction of what she wants. Wanting is common. Movement is rare. That's the entire game.

**How I Actually Practice It**

My version of the law of attraction is disciplined, not delusional.

I get crystal clear on the vision — specific enough that I can see it. Then I protect my mind like it's an asset, because it is. I don't feed it doubt, drama, or people who flinch at my goals. I speak my outcomes out loud before they're real, because language aims the brain. And I prove my discipline in the small things first: the carnivore diet, the gym, the 3am alarm. If I can keep my word to myself about a workout, I can keep it about a company. Discipline in one room leaks into every other room in the house.

Belief sets the destination. Discipline is the car. Action is the gas. You need all three or you go nowhere with a really nice vision board.

**The Foundation Under All of It**

I'm not doing this on willpower alone. My foundation is simple: me, my faith, and my three daughters — Valentina (14), Mili (12), and Scarlett (19 months) — plus Lucky, who never misses a 3am shift. I rely on myself, on God, and on the family I'm building this for.

When the doubt comes — and it comes — I don't argue with it. I out-work it. Then I hand the rest to God and go to sleep so I can do it again tomorrow.

**The Vision I'm Calling In**

I know exactly what I'm building toward, down to the detail. The brand on Sephora shelves. The dating clarity app sold. Part-time in Miami, surrounded by people who elevate me. Three daughters who grow up knowing their mother decided to be extraordinary and then did the work to back it up.

I can already see it. And every morning at 3am, I pay the rent on it.

That's the law of attraction nobody monetizes — because it asks you to do something. We're just getting started. 💸

title: From 0 to 3 Companies — What Nobody Tells You About Building While Raising Kids
excerpt: Building three companies as a single mom of three daughters taught me
body:
Everyone sees the vision board. Nobody sees the 3am work while the baby sleeps and the rest of the house has finally gone quiet.

I'm Lisa Haven — founder of **HAVENLY** ([www.havenly.co](https://www.havenly.co)), the makeup remover wipes brand built for Gen Z; **LUMAPROMPT.AI** ([www.lumaprompt.ai](https://www.lumaprompt.ai)), a premium prompt generator written for the way women actually think; and **VIXA** ([www.vixaapp.ai](https://www.vixaapp.ai)), the dating clarity app that hands women their power back. Three companies. Three daughters. One woman in Florida, building toward something that would make my girls proud.

**The Lie They Sell You**

They sell entrepreneurship like it's a highlight reel. One day you wake up, have a brilliant idea, pitch it, and *voilà* — you're on a Forbes list.

The real version? You're prepping carnivore meals on Sunday because there is no time to cook during the week. You're answering developer messages with one hand while feeding a 15-month-old with the other. And you carry all of it — the household, the companies, the vision — because that is exactly what you were built to do.

But you do it anyway. That's the whole thing.

**The Real Struggle Nobody Talks About: Focus**

Here is the part the founder podcasts skip. The hardest thing about building three companies while raising three daughters is not the strategy. It's not the capital. It's **focus** — finding uninterrupted, high-quality thinking time when your days belong to everyone but you.

Three kids. School runs. Meals. Laundry. A toddler who does not care that you have a paywall architecture to finalize. Every hour of my day is claimed before it begins.

So I built the one window that is entirely mine: **3am.**

When the house is silent — Lucky asleep at my feet, the only one who keeps me company at that hour — that is when I work. Not because I'm romanticizing the grind, but because that is the hour that belongs to me. That's when I do the deep work: the product decisions, the brand strategy, the thinking that actually moves a company forward. And it's when I learn. I study business operations courses. I study marketing. I watch founder stories until the sun comes up, pulling lessons from people who built empires from less than I have.

I'm not waiting to be taught. I'm teaching myself, one quiet morning at a time.

**Why Three?**

People ask why I started three companies at once. Honest answer: each one solves a problem I lived.

**HAVENLY** came from my obsession with skincare and noticing the wipe market hadn't been touched for Gen Z — the generation that actually reads ingredient lists and cares about aesthetics.

**LUMAPROMPT.AI** came from being frustrated with artificial intelligence tools — software that mimics human reasoning — that felt built by men, for men, producing outputs that missed the nuance of how women actually think and communicate.

**VIXA** came from too many conversations with girlfriends — brilliant, successful women — who were completely lost in the mixed signals of modern dating. We deserve clarity, not confusion.

**What Keeps Me Going**

My foundation is simple: me, my faith, my three daughters — Valentina (14), Mili (12), and Scarlett (15 months) — and Lucky, my dog, who's logged more 3am shifts beside me than anyone. I rely on myself, on God, and on the family I'm building this for.

My girls are watching everything. The discipline. The 3am alarm. The refusal to quit. I am raising three future bosses, and every choice I make is a lesson they're absorbing — that a woman builds her own life, on her own terms, and asks no one's permission to.

I am the one I count on. And that has been enough to build everything you see — with so much more still coming.

We're just getting started. 💸

title: Why I Went Carnivore — And How It Changed My Energy as a CEO Mom
excerpt: I needed something that would give me energy at 5am, clarity at noon, and still leave fuel in the tank for my daughters at 8pm. The carnivore diet did that.
body:
I know. I know. The first thing people say is: *"But where do you get your fiber?"*

And I smile, because six months ago I was exhausted, brain-fogged, and running three companies on cortisol and iced coffee. Now I wake up at 5am before my daughters, get my workout in, and have clarity that I haven't felt in years.

## What Is the Carnivore Diet?

Simple: meat, eggs, and water. That's essentially it. Some people add butter, some add salt. The premise is that animal products are the most nutrient-dense foods on earth and that many people do better eliminating plants entirely — especially those with autoimmune issues, gut problems, or chronic fatigue.

I'm not here to debate the science. I'm here to tell you what happened to my body.

## The First Two Weeks Were Brutal

I won't sugarcoat it. The adaptation period is rough — headaches, fatigue, crankiness. My body was a sugar-burner and it was not happy about the eviction notice.

By week three, something shifted. The brain fog I'd been carrying like a weighted blanket? Gone. The afternoon energy crash that had me reaching for a third espresso? Gone. I started sleeping deeply instead of anxiously.

## As a Busy Mom and CEO

Running a household with three daughters (one who is 15 months old and still waking up at night) while building three companies requires ENERGY. Not fake energy from stimulants — real, sustained energy.

Carnivore gave me that. I meal prep on Sundays: ground beef, eggs, steak, sometimes chicken. It takes 30 minutes and I'm fueled for the week without decision fatigue around food.

## Should You Try It?

Talk to your doctor. Seriously — this isn't for everyone and I'm not a nutritionist. But if you're chronically exhausted, inflamed, or running on empty, it might be worth investigating.

What I can tell you is that what you put in your body directly determines what you can pour out for your business, your kids, and your vision. 

For me, this was the answer. 🥩✨

title: I Built a Dating Clarity App Because I Was Tired of Group Chat Guesswork
excerpt: VIXA was born from one too many nights dissecting a 'lol' text with my
body:
You know the scene. Your phone buzzes. You screenshot the text. You send it to four different group chats. Everyone has a different theory. Two hours later you're more confused than when you started, and he's moved on with his evening completely unbothered.

We've all been there. I've been there. And as someone who was already building companies, I thought: *why is there no tool for this?*

That's how VIXA was born.

## What VIXA Actually Does

VIXA is an AI-powered dating clarity app built specifically for women. You paste in a conversation — or upload screenshots — and our AI companion Vela analyzes it. Not in a fluffy, vague way. In a *specific, actionable* way.

Vela reads:
- **Tone** — is he warm, distant, performative?
- **Timing** — response gaps, consistency patterns
- **Word choice** — effort level vs. minimum viable texting
- **Behavioral patterns** — breadcrumbing, love-bombing, genuine interest

She surfaces what's actually happening, scores the overall vibe, flags red flags, and generates reply suggestions that still sound like *you* — not a copied script from a Reddit thread.

## Why This Matters

Women are emotional. That's not a weakness — it's a superpower in most areas of life. But when it comes to analyzing someone who may or may not be wasting your time, emotions can cloud what the data is plainly showing.

VIXA gives you the clarity engine your best friend would be if she had absolutely no filter, perfect memory, and zero judgment.

## What's Coming

VIXA launches first for Apple iPhone with:
- **Free tier**: 10 analyses per week
- **Premium tier**: unlimited analyses, full script library, date-prep briefings, weekly behavioral pattern insights

We're building for the woman who is done wasting emotional energy. She deserves better information. She deserves VIXA.

Coming soon. Early access at [VIXAapp.ai](https://vixaapp.ai) 💗
